title: Private deployments: VPC & On‑Prem deployment guide, day‑2 ops, and rollback checklist
author: Samantha Lee
body:
Overview

This document is a consolidated, opinionated deployment guide for Redwood Private (VPC and on‑prem) focused on: deployment architecture, on‑prem packaging, networking prerequisites for VPC installations, day‑2 operational procedures, and deterministic upgrade & rollback steps. It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, and customer engineering teams executing an initial install or operating a production Private deployment.

Audience
- Platform / SRE engineers implementing Redwood Private in customer VPCs or on‑prem clusters.
- Solutions engineers validating customer requirements pre‑sale.

Goals
- Provide a repeatable deployment checklist and reference architecture.
- Enumerate day‑2 runbook items and monitoring thresholds.
- Define a safe, tested upgrade and rollback procedure.
- Document minimal customer requirements and suggested sizing profiles.

High‑level architecture
- Control plane: customer‑managed control plane in a dedicated management VPC (for VPC installs) or a management VLAN (on‑prem). Contains: config server, license service, and audit‑logging forwarder.
- Data plane: compute nodes hosting inference runtime (GPU hosts) and optional replica serving nodes.
- Network segmentation: separate management, control, and serving subnets; strict egress rules for model download and telemetry.

Reference deployment topologies
1) Small (POC) — 1 control plane node, 2 inference nodes (1 GPU), single AZ: suitable for evals and limited internal workloads.
2) Production (HA) — 3 control plane nodes across 2+ AZs, 4–8 inference nodes (GPUs sized to model family), dedicated storage cluster for model artifacts and KV cache.
3) Regulated (air‑gapped) — control plane deployed on customer network with KMS/HSM integration, artifact transfer via signed USB bundles or private registry mirror.

Networking & VPC requirements (checklist)
- Subnets: management (private), control (private), serving (private).
- CIDR sizing: recommend /24 per subnet for medium deployments.
- Security groups / NACLs: allow inbound from internal monitoring CIDRs; control plane <-> data plane TCP 443, 8443; inference grpc/TCP ports as documented below.
- Ports: 443 (control API), 8443 (internal control), 50051 (gRPC runtime), 9100 (node exporter), 9200 (es proxy if used).
- NAT/Egress: control plane must be able to reach model catalog endpoints and OS package repos (or use mirror).
- PrivateLink / VPC endpoints: optional for tightening egress to Redwood artifact registries.

On‑prem packaging & install mediums
- Packaging options: container images (recommended), VM appliance (OVA), or bare‑metal installer (RPM/DEB + systemd).
- Image registry: customers should mirror Redwood container images to a private registry (Harbor/ECR) for air‑gapped installs.
- Artifact verification: SHA256 checksums and signed manifests are included in release bundles. Verify prior to install: sha256sum -c RELEASES.sha256.
- Storage requirements (per node): minimum 200 GB SSD for OS + runtime; recommended 1–2 TB NVMe for model storage on inference nodes for medium/large models.

Customer requirements matrix (short summary table)
- Minimal compute: 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM per control node; inference nodes sized per model (see quantization profiles doc).
- GPU types: recommended NVIDIA A10/A100 or equivalent; for INT8/4bit quantized workloads, T4/A10 are acceptable with quantization profile adjustments.
- Network: 1 Gbps for small; 10 Gbps recommended for production GPU clusters.
- Storage: low latency SSD for model artifacts and KV cache.

Sample configuration snippet (Kubernetes manifests / container install example)
- Example: control plane service (k8s) YAML excerpt (replace image tags and registry):

apiVersion: v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: redwood-control
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: control
        image: my-registry.local/redwood/control:2026.06.01
        env:
        - name: REDWOOD_K8S_MODE
          value: "true"

(Full manifests live in the packaging repo; contact devops for private repo access.)

Day‑2 operations (runbook & procedures)
- Daily checks (automated where possible):
  1) Control plane API health: /healthz returns 200, latency < 200ms.
  2) Model cache hit ratio: aim > 80% for steady workloads.
  3) Queue latency: request queue > 95th percentile < 250ms for sync requests.
  4) GPU utilization: steady state 40–70%; sustained > 90% indicates undersizing.
- Weekly tasks:
  - Rotate audit logging keys if using external forwarders.
  - Run canary prompts set to detect model regressions (link to prompt‑sets-and‑benchmarks).
- Incident triage steps (high level):
  1) Identify scope: control plane only vs inference degradation.
  2) If control plane degraded: check etcd/postgres health, control leader election, and API logs.
  3) If inference degraded: check GPU drivers, nvml errors, and model disk I/O.
  4) For persistent node faults: cordon + drain (k8s) or remove from load balancer and initiate replacement.

Monitoring & SLOs (suggested)
- API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for control API (customer SLA depends on contract).
- Per‑request latency targets: median < 100ms for short prompts (< 64 tokens); p95 < 700ms.
- Error budget handling: if > 0.1% 5xx errors over a 6‑hour window, trigger immediate incident engagement.

Upgrade procedure (safe path)
1) Pre‑upgrade validation:
   - Run health check script: tools/deploy/check_health.sh (must return OK).
   - Snapshot control plane DB: pg_dump + store in versioned bucket.
   - Ensure runbook for model artifact migration is reviewed.
2) Canary rollout:
   - Deploy new control plane version to 1 node (canary) and run smoke tests (API, auth, telemetry).
   - If canary green for 30 minutes and no errors, proceed.
3) Rolling upgrade:
   - Upgrade control plane nodes one at a time; ensure quorum and leader election succeed between steps.
   - Upgrade inference nodes in small batches (10–20% of capacity), monitor latency and error rates.
4) Post‑upgrade validation:
   - Run end‑to‑end inference tests and model correctness checks (predefined prompt set).
   - Verify KV cache rebuild and warming; ensure cache hit ratio returns to expected levels.

Rollback procedure (if upgrade fails)
1) Criteria for rollback: increase in 5xx errors >0.5% or p95 latency degradation > 2x baseline for > 15 minutes.
2) Immediate actions:
   - Stop further rollout.
   - Rollback canary node image to previous tag and validate.
3) If systemic failure:
   - Initiate full rollback of control plane using DB snapshot and prior container images.
   - For inference nodes: restore previous image and clear model cache if corrupted (rm -rf /var/lib/redwood/model-cache/* and restart runtime).
4) Post‑rollback diagnostics:
   - Collect logs from control and inference nodes (journalctl, container logs).
   - Open a postmortem and tag release with failure reason.

Operational checklist (pre‑deployment)
- Confirm customer requirements and signoff (network, storage, KMS).
- Validate image registry access and checksum verification.
- Confirm monitoring/alerting targets and Slack/email escalation routes.
- Ensure runbook and rollback steps are documented and accessible to oncall.

Runbook: common tasks (commands & quick procedures)
- Verify control API: curl -sSf -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://control.internal.redwood.local/healthz
- Check GPU driver: nvidia-smi -q | grep "Driver Version"
- Restart control service (systemd): sudo systemctl restart redwood-control
- Drain node (k8s): kubectl cordon NODE && kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data

Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments team (oncall: #private‑deployments)
- Secondary: eng-sre for alerts and capacity planning
- Packaging & releases: eng-infra release manager (contact in related_pages)

Appendices
A) Sizing examples (medium production): 3x control (8 vCPU, 32GB), 6x inference (each: 24 vCPU, 192GB, 2x A10), dedicated SSD model store (12TB).
B) Troubleshooting quick reference: list of common log paths, error patterns and playbook links.

Notes & further reading
- See packaging repo for full manifests and example installers.
- See quantization-profiles and eval-harness pages for model performance tuning and validation.
